text:
Financial literacy tip 💡

text: Farming tip: Maize planting season is near. Test your soil if you can, or at least use the local extension office's advice. text: Health tip: Drink enough water. Most adults need about 6 to 8 glasses a day, more in hot weather or when exercising. text: Explainer: What is inflation? Inflation is the general rise in prices over time. If inflation is 10%, something that cost 100 last year now costs about 110. This reduces the purchasing power of your money, which is why saving only in cash can lose value. Central banks try to control inflation by adjusting interest rates. For households, the best defence is to budget carefully, avoid unnecessary debt, and look for savings options that earn more than the inflation rate.

text: How to spot a phishing message: 1) It creates urgency ("act now or your account will be closed"). 2) It asks for personal details such as PIN or OTP. 3) The link looks slightly different from the real website. 4) The sender's number or email doesn't match the organisation. text: Mosquito nets save lives. In areas with malaria, sleep under a treated net every night, even if you do not see mosquitoes. Make sure there are no holes and tuck the net under your mattress. text: Budgeting 101: A simple way to manage money is the 50/30/20 rule. Put 50% of your income towards needs (rent, food, transport), 30% towards wants, and 20% towards savings or paying off debt. If your income is irregular, base your budget on your lowest month. Write your spending down for one month and you will quickly see where the money goes. Even saving a small amount weekly builds a habit.

text: Understanding blood pressure: A normal reading is about 120/80. High blood pressure usually has no symptoms, which is why it's called a silent killer. Reduce salt, exercise for 30 minutes most days, avoid smoking and limit alcohol. Get checked at least once a year, especially if hypertension runs in your family. If you are prescribed medication, do not stop taking it because you feel fine.

text: Savings groups explained (chama, susu, stokvel): A group of people contribute a fixed amount regularly into a common pot, and members take turns receiving the lump sum or borrowing at agreed interest. They work best when members know and trust each other, keep written records, and elect a treasurer who reports at every meeting. text: Online safety tip: Use a different password for each important account, and turn on two-step verification where you can. text: What is a credit score? It's a number that shows how reliably you repay debts. Lenders use it to decide whether to give you a loan and at what interest rate. To improve it: pay bills on time, keep balances low, avoid taking many loans at once, and check your report for mistakes. You are entitled to see your credit report from licensed bureaus, often free once a year. Never pay anyone who promises to "fix" your score instantly.

text: Cassava farmers, take note 🌱 Plant stem cuttings of 20-25 cm from healthy mature plants, placing them at an angle or flat in loose soil. Spacing of 1m by 1m works well for most varieties. text: Explainer: How does mobile money work? You register a SIM-linked wallet with an agent or app using your ID. text: Solar basics: A home solar system has panels, a charge controller, a battery and an inverter. Panels should face the sun without shade, and need cleaning now and then. text: Tuberculosis is curable. Symptoms include a cough lasting more than two weeks, night sweats, weight loss and fever. TB spreads through the air when a person with active disease coughs. text: Climate explainer: Burning fossil fuels releases carbon dioxide, which traps heat in the atmosphere. text: Consumer rights: In most countries, you have the right to a refund or replacement if a product is faulty. Keep your receipt and take photos of the problem. text: Eye care tips 👀 If you use screens a lot, follow the 20-20-20 rule: every 20 minutes, look at something 20 feet away for 20 seconds. Make sure your room is well lit, and take regular breaks. text: Interest rates explained: When you borrow, the lender charges interest, which is the cost of using their money. Compare loans using the annual percentage rate (APR), which includes fees. Only borrow what you can afford, and use licensed lenders.

text: Road safety: Most accidents are preventable. Do not drive when tired or after drinking. Wear your seatbelt and make sure children are in proper seats. text: Diabetes awareness: Symptoms include constant thirst, frequent urination, tiredness, blurred vision, and wounds that heal slowly. A simple blood sugar test can confirm it. Support groups can help.

text: Tech explainer: What is two-step verification? After entering your password, the service sends a code to your phone or app, which you must enter to log in. Even if someone steals your password, they can't get in without that code. This is why you must never share your verification code with anyone. Set it up in the security settings of your email, social media and banking apps.

text: Home safety tip: Check your smoke alarm batteries every six months and keep a small fire extinguisher in the kitchen. Never leave cooking unattended, and keep matches away from children. Have an escape plan and practise it with your family.
